title: On The Regularized McVittie Black Bounce and a Family of Traversable Wormholes
summary: The McVittie metric describes a self-gravitating compact object embedded in an expanding universe. It inherits two singularities: a curvature singularity at $r \to 0$ and a cosmological singularity at $a(t) \to 0$. Motivated by the construction of black-bounce geometries, we regularize both of these singularities and propose a regularized McVittie metric. The central singularity is regularized by replacing $r \to \sqrt{r^{2}+b^{2}}$, leading to a geometry that interpolates between a cosmological black hole, a black bounce, and a traversable wormhole.
